paragraphs.en: The Ballmer Peak is a humorous concept invented by Randall Munroe in the xkcd webcomic , joking that a programmer who is appropriately intoxicated (between 0.129-0.138% BAC ) will achieve a high level of programming productivity ; the peak occurs at 0.1337%, a reference to leet . The concept is loosely tied to former Microsoft CEO, Steve Ballmer , [ 1 ] [ 2 ] and is likely a play on Balmer series of hydrogen spectral lines named for the scientist Johann Balmer . [ 3 ]
paragraphs.zh: 「巴尔默峰值」（Ballmer Peak）是兰德尔·门罗（Randall Munroe）在 xkcd 网络漫画中发明的幽默概念，开玩笑说程序员在适度饮酒（血液酒精浓度在 0.129%-0.138% 之间）时能达到极高的编程效率；该峰值出现在 0.1337%，是对「leet」（精英黑客用语）的致敬。 这一概念松散地关联到微软前首席执行官史蒂夫·鲍尔默（Steve Ballmer），[ 1 ] [ 2 ] 并且很可能是对以科学家约翰·巴尔默（Johann Balmer）命名的氢原子光谱线「巴尔默系」（Balmer series）的文字游戏。[ 3 ]

sents.en: The concept is loosely tied to former Microsoft CEO, Steve Ballmer , [ 1 ] [ 2 ] and is likely a play on Balmer series of hydrogen spectral lines named for the scientist Johann Balmer . [ 3 ]
sents.zh: 这一概念松散地关联到微软前首席执行官史蒂夫·鲍尔默（Steve Ballmer），[ 1 ] [ 2 ] 并且很可能是对以科学家约翰·巴尔默（Johann Balmer）命名的氢原子光谱线「巴尔默系」（Balmer series）的文字游戏。[ 3 ]

paragraphs.en: A San Francisco organization, Originate, has organized a "Ballmer Peak-A-Thon", an open bar event where people were given "5 hours to find the elusive Ballmer peak, and build the best worst business possible." [ 2 ] [ 4 ]
paragraphs.zh: 旧金山的一个组织 Originate 曾举办过一场「鲍尔默峰值马拉松」（Ballmer Peak-A-Thon），这是一个开放式酒吧活动，参与者有「5 个小时的时间去寻找那难以捉摸的鲍尔默峰值，并构建出最棒的最糟糕生意」。 [ 2 ] [ 4 ]

paragraphs.en: There is no scientific basis for the Ballmer Peak, though researchers have studied adjacent topics, such as the impact of inebriation on problem solving . [ 5 ] One study identified worse programming performance with increasing blood alcohol content , but joked in a footnote that as "the prescribed BAC in this experiment did not reach the Ballmer Peak", they did not technically refute the concept. [ 6 ] In addition, the Ballmer Peak has been the subject of satirical academic studies, including a 2024 paper presented at SIGBOVIK , a satirical computer science conference organized by Carnegie Mellon students, [ 7 ] which caught broader attention in the programming community. [ 8 ] That study, which tested blood alcohol levels of only one male subject tackling competitive computer programming questions, found no evidence of a sudden "peak" of programming ability but did generally find that speed of solving the challenges increased with some alcohol consumption before a rapid decline. [ 7 ]
paragraphs.zh: 「鲍尔默峰值」并没有科学依据，不过研究人员已经研究过相邻的课题，例如醉酒对解决问题的影响。 [ 5 ] 一项研究发现，随着血液酒精含量的升高，编程表现会变差，但该研究在脚注中开玩笑说，由于“本实验设定的血液酒精浓度并未达到鲍尔默峰值”，因此在严格意义上并没有驳倒这一概念。 [ 6 ] 此外，鲍尔默峰值还成为了一些讽刺性学术研究的主题，其中包括一篇于2024年发表在SIGBOVIK上的论文，SIGBOVIK是由卡内基梅隆大学学生组织的讽刺性计算机科学会议，[ 7 ] 这篇论文引起了编程界的广泛关注。 [ 8 ] 该研究仅测试了一名男性受试者在解答竞赛编程题目时的血液酒精水平，结果发现没有任何证据表明编程能力会突然出现“峰值”，但总体上发现，在摄入一定量的酒精后，解题速度有所提升，随后又迅速下降。[ 7 ]

paragraphs.en: By the time of Ballmer's 2013 announcement of his retirement from Microsoft, the concept of the "Ballmer Peak" was entrenched enough that media joked that the actual Ballmer Peak was the resulting jump in stock price. [ 9 ]
paragraphs.zh: 到2013年鲍尔默宣布从微软退休时，「鲍尔默峰值」这一概念已经深入人心，以至于媒体打趣说，真正的鲍尔默峰值是此举引发的股价上涨。 [ 9 ]
